title: PayPal, webhooks, refunds, and idempotency
summary: Build payments where the server controls amounts, verifies events, and withstands retries and partial refunds.

lessons.title: PayPal order lifecycle
prerequisites: Understand minor currency units, database transactions, authenticated server calls, and that a webhook may be delivered more than once.
Be able to restate “capture” before coding: The step that turns an approved authorization into a confirmed transfer of funds.
Know how to create exercises/22-payments/paypal-order.ts, run npm run build, and compare real output with a written expectation.
objectives: Calculate the amount on the server, create a provider order, obtain customer approval, then capture and reconcile the internal reference.

Build a deterministic PayPal payload whose reference connects payment to the L’ecomax cart, then prove the result with this exact signal: the payload contains the internal reference, USD, and the two-decimal server value; changing the browser total does not change it.

blocks.text: The payment provider confirms movement of money; the store remains responsible for price, its internal order, and the allowed state transition. In “PayPal order lifecycle”, the concrete input is a cart whose server reloads products and prices, creates an internal order, then sends PayPal an explicitly named USD amount. capture means: The step that turns an approved authorization into a confirmed transfer of funds. The model is complete only when you keep amount and currency as one business value, use a PayPal currency actually configured for the account, and never convert by renaming a variable and can observe that the payload contains the internal reference, USD, and the two-decimal server value; changing the browser total does not change it.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Payment is like checking a ticket: the traveler’s screen is not proof; only signed validation reconciled with the record permits entry. Here the part you will actually inspect is a deterministic PayPal payload whose reference connects payment to the L’ecomax cart; stop using the analogy if it obscures the technical boundary shown by the code.

Start by bounding this lesson’s case: a cart whose server reloads products and prices, creates an internal order, then sends PayPal an explicitly named USD amount. Calculate the amount on the server, create a provider order, obtain customer approval, then capture and reconcile the internal reference. The term capture is not a decorative label: The step that turns an approved authorization into a confirmed transfer of funds. It determines what enters, which authority may act, and which observation counts as evidence rather than an impression.

In exercises/22-payments/paypal-order.ts, the example deliberately reduces the system to a deterministic PayPal payload whose reference connects payment to the L’ecomax cart. Read each line as one responsibility, then run npm run build. The main failure to trigger is: a totalMAD field is copied into currency_code USD without conversion or commercial agreement, charging an amount in the wrong currency. It shows why the professional correction is to keep amount and currency as one business value, use a PayPal currency actually configured for the account, and never convert by renaming a variable, not to conceal the error.

In a real system, the happy path is only one case among retries, invalid input, and partial outages. The expected proof is that the payload contains the internal reference, USD, and the two-decimal server value; changing the browser total does not change it. Apply the same evidence to order creation, PayPal capture, refunds, and stock updates, using a correlation trace without secrets or personal data so both success and failure remain explainable.

items.definition: The step that turns an approved authorization into a confirmed transfer of funds.

objectives: Validate amount and reason, link the refund to the original capture, and retain identifiers for every transition for support and accounting.

Build a bounded refund request that rejects impossible amounts before any network call, then prove the result with this exact signal: the server rejects zero, negative, and excessive values, records reason and actor, then reconciles the confirmed refund identifier.

blocks.text: The payment provider confirms movement of money; the store remains responsible for price, its internal order, and the allowed state transition. In “Refunds and reconciliation”, the concrete input is a partial-refund request tied to an existing USD capture and the sum of already confirmed refunds. reconciliation means: Comparison of internal records with provider records to detect financial discrepancies. The model is complete only when you compute refundable balance in a transaction, retain capture currency, use a request key, and record an immutable audit and can observe that the server rejects zero, negative, and excessive values, records reason and actor, then reconciles the confirmed refund identifier.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Payment is like checking a ticket: the traveler’s screen is not proof; only signed validation reconciled with the record permits entry. Here the part you will actually inspect is a bounded refund request that rejects impossible amounts before any network call; stop using the analogy if it obscures the technical boundary shown by the code.

Start by bounding this lesson’s case: a partial-refund request tied to an existing USD capture and the sum of already confirmed refunds. Validate amount and reason, link the refund to the original capture, and retain identifiers for every transition for support and accounting. The term reconciliation is not a decorative label: Comparison of internal records with provider records to detect financial discrepancies. It determines what enters, which authority may act, and which observation counts as evidence rather than an impression.

In exercises/22-payments/refund.ts, the example deliberately reduces the system to a bounded refund request that rejects impossible amounts before any network call. Read each line as one responsibility, then run npx tsc --noEmit. The main failure to trigger is: two agents each refund the captured amount because validation ignores previous refunds and concurrency. It shows why the professional correction is to compute refundable balance in a transaction, retain capture currency, use a request key, and record an immutable audit, not to conceal the error.

In a real system, the happy path is only one case among retries, invalid input, and partial outages. The expected proof is that the server rejects zero, negative, and excessive values, records reason and actor, then reconciles the confirmed refund identifier. Apply the same evidence to order creation, PayPal capture, refunds, and stock updates, using a correlation trace without secrets or personal data so both success and failure remain explainable.
